item.title: Last Marine Harrier jet arrives at Pensacola museum after final mission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The final AV-8B Harrier jet ever produced for the U.S. Marine Corps has completed its last flight and been delivered to the National Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola for permanent display. Bureau Number 166288 arrived at the museum after being demilitarized and made safe for static exhibition, marking the end of an era for the iconic…
item.content:encoded:
The final AV-8B Harrier jet ever produced for the U.S. Marine Corps has completed its last flight and been delivered to the National Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola for permanent display. Bureau Number 166288 arrived at the museum after being demilitarized and made safe for static exhibition, marking the end of an era for the iconic vertical-takeoff aircraft.

The jet, delivered by Boeing in September 2003, accumulated more than 5,800 flight hours during its operational service, including multiple combat deployments. The Harrier's unique ability to take off and land vertically made it a cornerstone of Marine air operations for decades, though the service has since transitioned to the newer F-35B Lightning II fighter.

The museum's acquisition of BuNo 166288 adds a significant piece to its collection of naval aviation history. The National Naval Aviation Museum, located at Naval Air Station Pensacola, preserves and displays aircraft and artifacts spanning more than a century of naval flight operations. The Harrier's arrival underscores the museum's role in honoring the aircraft and aviators that have shaped Marine and Navy aviation.

item.title: ECPS, Magdalene's Host Free Online Safety Workshop for Parents, Kids
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Public Schools is teaming up with local anti-trafficking organization Magdalene's, Inc. to offer a free community education event on the dangers children face online, with two session dates scheduled for mid-October. The workshop, titled "Playing It Safe: Exposing Dangers in Our Digital World," will bring together school district…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools is teaming up with local anti-trafficking organization Magdalene's, Inc. to offer a free community education event on the dangers children face online, with two session dates scheduled for mid-October.

The workshop, titled "Playing It Safe: Exposing Dangers in Our Digital World," will bring together school district leaders, law enforcement, and Dr. Andrew Doan, an expert in media addiction, to discuss the risks young people encounter through smartphones, gaming, social media, and other internet activity. According to the district, over 500,000 online predators are active at any given time, making digital safety education critical for parents, guardians, educators, and community members.

The event is designed for ages 13 and up and will cover what children encounter online, current protections in place within ECPS, and practical steps families can take if they spot suspicious activity. "The No. 1 priority of Escambia County Public Schools is to protect our students," the district said in announcing the partnership.

Two identical sessions are scheduled for October 13 and October 15. Seating is limited, and registration is encouraged through Eventbrite. The event is free and open to all community members. More information and registration links are available through the school district.

A historic aircraft has completed its two-week journey from Pensacola to the Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum in Colorado, arriving Wednesday at its new home.

According to KKTV 11 News, the plane made the cross-country trek from Pensacola, marking a significant transfer for the historic aircraft. The Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum, located in Colorado, specializes in restoring and preserving vintage and historic aircraft.

Details about the specific aircraft type and its historical significance were not immediately available, but the long-distance delivery highlights the logistical challenges involved in moving historic aviation treasures across the country.

item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority is reminding customers they have until Thursday, September 30 to complete the 2026 Customer Survey, according to a release from the utility.

The survey gives ECUA customers a chance to share feedback on service, billing, and other aspects of the utility's operations. Participation helps the authority understand what's working well and where improvements may be needed.

Customers can find the survey through ECUA's website or may receive information about participating by mail. With just over a week left before the deadline, ECUA is encouraging anyone who hasn't yet filled out the brief questionnaire to do so before September 30.

item.content:encoded:
Calder Allen has found his own way to channel the constant stream of thoughts running through his mind—two pursuits that ground him in the present moment.

According to reporting in InWeekly, Allen relies on fly fishing and songwriting as outlets to organize his ideas and creative energy. While he acknowledges he can't quiet the mental noise entirely, both activities give him a sense of direction and purpose.

The combination of outdoor recreation and artistic expression provides Allen with a way to transform what could otherwise feel overwhelming into something productive and meaningful. For many people juggling multiple interests, finding those two or three anchors can make all the difference in managing daily life.

Allen's approach—leaning into what works rather than fighting against his nature—offers a practical reminder that our supposed weaknesses sometimes just need the right outlet.

Pensacola Bay Area's IMPACT 100 program has selected 20 finalists competing for nonprofit grants ahead of the organization's annual meeting on October 11, with 13 organizations expected to receive $101,000 in total awards.

The record number of finalists and payout reflect strong membership participation in the giving circle, which pools donations from local women to fund community nonprofits. The Oct. 11 gathering will determine which finalists receive funding as part of the 2026 cycle.

IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area connects women donors with vetted local nonprofits addressing education, health, economic empowerment, and other community priorities. Details on the 20 finalists and the selection criteria are expected to be available through the organization ahead of the October meeting.

item.title: Hollice T. Williams Park aims to restore Pensacola neighborhood severed by I-110
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: For decades, Interstate 110 has been a physical scar across Pensacola's landscape—a reminder of a thriving neighborhood that was dismantled to make way for the highway. Now, Hollice T. Williams Park is working to reconnect residents with the history and community that once defined the area before the interstate cut through it. According to…
item.content:encoded:
For decades, Interstate 110 has been a physical scar across Pensacola's landscape—a reminder of a thriving neighborhood that was dismantled to make way for the highway. Now, Hollice T. Williams Park is working to reconnect residents with the history and community that once defined the area before the interstate cut through it.

According to reporting in InWeekly, the park represents an effort to honor what was lost when I-110 was constructed. The area that now surrounds the park was once home to a vibrant neighborhood with residential streets, churches, and local businesses—the kind of interconnected community spaces that gave the area its character and identity.

The initiative signals a shift toward acknowledging Pensacola's past and the impact that mid-century infrastructure decisions had on established neighborhoods. By reclaiming and reimagining public space, the park offers a chance for residents to rebuild some of the connections that were severed when the highway divided the community.

Hollywood's summer run delivered a blockbuster performance, according to InWeekly's fall movie preview. The domestic box office crossed the $4 billion mark and exceeded pre-pandemic revenue levels, signaling strong audience appetite for theatrical releases as the industry heads into the fall season.

The robust summer numbers suggest Americans are returning to movie theaters in force, a trend that could carry momentum into the coming months as studios prepare their autumn slate. Industry analysts will be watching closely to see whether fall releases can maintain the summer's pace.

For Pensacola-area moviegoers looking ahead, the fall season typically brings a mix of franchise sequels, prestige dramas, and holiday-targeted family films. More details on what's coming to local theaters will emerge as studios finalize their release schedules.

The case has drawn attention across state lines, with local interest given the connections between the individuals involved. The grand jury's ruling stands as a significant development in what has been an ongoing matter for Wells' family and friends seeking accountability.

Orange Beach Fire Rescue is investigating two house fires on Ono Island that occurred within 12 hours of each other — one Tuesday night and another early Wednesday morning, according to WKRG News 5.

Firefighters responded to both blazes, though the exact cause of either fire has not been determined. The rapid succession of the two incidents has prompted investigators to examine whether the fires are connected.

Ono Island, located in Baldwin County near Orange Beach, Alabama, is a residential community across the bay from the Pensacola area. Details about damage, injuries, or the identity of the affected properties have not yet been released. The investigation remains ongoing as fire officials work to determine what sparked each fire.

item.title: Taddeo, Former CFO Sink Rally Support as Florida's CFO Race Deadlocked
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Democratic nominee Annette Taddeo is bringing in heavyweight support as the race for Florida Chief Financial Officer remains competitive heading into the final stretch. Former CFO Alex Sink will join Taddeo for a virtual press conference Thursday morning to discuss recent polling showing the race tied at 42% each for Taddeo and Republican Blaise…
item.content:encoded:
Democratic nominee Annette Taddeo is bringing in heavyweight support as the race for Florida Chief Financial Officer remains competitive heading into the final stretch. Former CFO Alex Sink will join Taddeo for a virtual press conference Thursday morning to discuss recent polling showing the race tied at 42% each for Taddeo and Republican Blaise Ingoglia, with 16% of voters still undecided.

The campaign is banking on a specific electoral playbook: winning independent voters. According to the latest survey, Taddeo leads among voters with no party affiliation by 12 points—a margin that echoes Sink's successful 2006 campaign for the same office. That year, Sink trailed overall in October polling but won the general election after dominating with independent voters by 11 points. "Twenty years later, we're seeing similar dynamics," a campaign statement noted.

Taddeo is also pressing the accountability angle, calling for a legislative investigation into taxpayer-funded criminal defense legal fees for the Chief of Staff of Republican rival Ingoglia, citing questions about financial oversight and the CFO's responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars. The press conference, scheduled for 9:45 a.m. Thursday via Zoom, will focus on independent voter dynamics, the latest polling, and Taddeo's platform of affordability, accountability, and anti-corruption.

item.title: Santa Rosa County opens free hazmat disposal day Saturday in Gulf Breeze
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County residents can drop off household hazardous waste and old tires free of charge this Saturday, October 10, at the South Santa Rosa Service Center in Gulf Breeze. The event runs from 8 a.m. to noon at 5841 Gulf Breeze Parkway and lets residents dispose of materials that shouldn't go in regular trash without making the drive to the…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County residents can drop off household hazardous waste and old tires free of charge this Saturday, October 10, at the South Santa Rosa Service Center in Gulf Breeze. The event runs from 8 a.m. to noon at 5841 Gulf Breeze Parkway and lets residents dispose of materials that shouldn't go in regular trash without making the drive to the Central Landfill in Milton.

Accepted items include up to 10 car or truck tires per vehicle (no commercial or heavy-duty tires), five gallons each of antifreeze, gasoline, paint, solvents, and oil, batteries, propane bottles, pool chemicals, electronics like flat-screen TVs and computers, and fluorescent light bulbs. The county also accepts used sharps containers and will provide free replacements. Residents should bring a valid photo ID to prove Santa Rosa County residency.

Due to new state requirements, tire disposal now requires pre-registration. Residents can sign up online at SantaRosa.fl.gov/Tires or complete a form at the event. Small businesses and schools can also dispose of hazardous waste at a reduced rate by appointment; call (850) 981-7135 by noon the day before to schedule. The program is funded by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection in cooperation with Okaloosa County.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Animal Services: $10 Adoptions End Sept. 30
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Animal Services is in the final week of a nationwide adoption promotion offering dramatically reduced fees on cats and dogs. Through Wednesday, September 30, the shelter at 4451 Pine Forest Road in Milton is charging just $10 per animal as part of BISSELL Pet Foundation's Empty the Shelters event. All available pets at the…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Animal Services is in the final week of a nationwide adoption promotion offering dramatically reduced fees on cats and dogs. Through Wednesday, September 30, the shelter at 4451 Pine Forest Road in Milton is charging just $10 per animal as part of BISSELL Pet Foundation's Empty the Shelters event.

All available pets at the shelter come already spayed or neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped. "This is a great opportunity for anyone who has been thinking about adding a pet to their family," said Santa Rosa County Animal Services Chief Randy Lambert. "There's only one week left, and there are so many wonderful cats and dogs waiting for their chance to go home."

The Empty the Shelters initiative, now in its second decade, has helped nearly 400,000 animals find homes across the U.S. and Canada since launching in 2016. The program coordinates with hundreds of shelters and rescue organizations to ease capacity pressures. Santa Rosa County Animal Services alone handles roughly 3,500 animals annually that arrive lost, displaced, or in need of care.

Prospective adopters can browse available animals online at www.santarosa.fl.gov/Animals or visit the shelter in person during operating hours. With the deadline just seven days away, the shelter is urging interested families to act soon.

item.title: Mayor Reeves: Airport Hits 485-Day Streak, New Traffic Signals Coming for Emergency Vehicles
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola International Airport has now gone 485 days without a wait longer than 30 minutes at TSA screening, Mayor D.C. Reeves told Pensacola's Morning News this week — a streak he says traces back to a federal staffing fix pushed through with help from Senator Rick Scott's office. Reeves also addressed lingering…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Pensacola International Airport has now gone 485 days without a wait longer than 30 minutes at TSA screening, Mayor D.C. Reeves told Pensacola's Morning News this week — a streak he says traces back to a federal staffing fix pushed through with help from Senator Rick Scott's office. Reeves also addressed lingering questions about last month's Palafox Street flooding, detailed a new traffic signal upgrade aimed at emergency vehicles, and gave an update on a citizen engagement portal that's drawn tens of thousands of votes from residents.


Airport Marks 485 Days Without a Major TSA Wait

Reeves says the airport has gone roughly 7,300 consecutive hours — measured hour by hour, not just day by day — without a security wait topping 30 minutes. That stretch covers close to 5 million passengers and about 2.5 million security screenings during a period of steadily growing traffic through the airport.


The streak follows a rough patch a while back, when long TSA lines became a regular complaint. Reeves says the city's "mild complaints" escalated after a particularly bad stretch prompted a letter to federal officials, and Senator Rick Scott's office responded with what Reeves called an emergency deployment — eight additional TSA staff sent to Pensacola within a day. A closer look afterward found the airport had been understaffed by about 30 percent, Reeves says, a gap he attributes to passenger growth outpacing federal staffing levels. The airport has since added extra screening capacity, including what Reeves believes is an additional screening lane.


City Explains Palafox Flooding, Points to Undersized FDOT Pipe


Reeves pushed back on characterizations of last month's downtown flooding as a city failure, calling it instead a win for the city's stormwater design. He says standing water during the storm was limited to one block of Palafox Street — between Garden and Romana — for about 15 minutes, with zero water intrusion into any downtown businesses, in a storm that he says historically would have caused sandbagging and flooded shops.

Reeves says the bottleneck traces to a Florida Department of Transportation-owned pipe under Garden Street that the city doesn't control. He says the city has known the pipe was undersized since at least 2015 and again in 2019, but its options were limited to leaving the first block of Palafox without stormwater improvements or routing water into the undersized FDOT pipe. "It just means the pipe is undersized," Reeves said. "That's the issue."

New Traffic Signals to Give Emergency Vehicles the Green Light


The city is upgrading traffic signals along 9th Avenue, Cervantes Street and Scenic Highway to work with its Advanced Traffic Management System, a roughly $1 million project funded by FDOT. The upgrade will let the city turn every light along a corridor green for emergency responders heading to a call.

Reeves says the technology has been in the works since he took office, but development has moved fast enough that emergency vehicles themselves may soon be able to trigger green lights directly — without needing to request the change through the city's traffic management office.

Online Portal Draws 65,000 Votes on City Issues


Reeves says a citizen engagement portal launched through the city's partnership with the U.S. Conference of Mayors has drawn about 65,000 votes on roughly 1,200 submitted ideas. The platform allows residents to submit and vote on concerns and ideas for the city, and Reeves says the process is designed to end in solutions-based recommendations rather than simply cataloging complaints.


Because submissions are open to anyone, some ideas posted to the portal fall outside city jurisdiction — Reeves pointed to a submission about fixing drainage on Nine Mile Road, which isn't in city limits, as one example. He says those outliers are expected in an open forum and get filtered out as the platform identifies the most common and widely supported themes. The city plans to bring together and pay about 100 residents to workshop the top issues that emerge and develop concrete recommendations.
